identity_input_diagnostic.diagnostic: matched base versus identity-policy recorded-input divergence
identity_input_diagnostic.interpretation: Observed divergence does not by itself identify physics, rendering, batching, or numerical inference as the cause. No changes to scientific inputs or selection rules.

report.selection_rule: Three largest saved parity errors among failed items, then first three passed items by original capture order
report.method: Repeat the identical observation and sampling seed 16 times to isolate batch shape without changing inputs; compare first output. Saved instrumented actions are not rerun.

coordinate_audit.selection_rule: Three largest saved parity errors among failed items, then first three passed items by original capture order
interpretation: These six selected requests from five episodes compare fixed recorded inputs and sampling seeds; they are not independent trials or a frequency estimate.

Native batch16 reproduces saved live actions closely; native batch1 is repeatable but differs. This supports batch-shape-dependent numerical execution as the dominant source of the selected raw-output replay discrepancy.
All three selected saved-parity failures have their largest batch1/batch16 discrepancy in raw gripper column7. None of the90 compared action rows changes the binary gripper decision at threshold0.5.
The original replay gate uses the maximum over mixed joint-command and raw-gripper coordinates. A failed raw-output check need not imply a changed binary gripper decision.
Joint commands also differ. This diagnostic contains no new closed-loop rollouts and does not establish that batching caused episode failures or identity-repeat outcome changes.
Initial camera-input differences in the separate identity-repeat audit are a distinct observation and are not explained by this fixed-input diagnostic.
The batch16 repeats one input16times and compares position0; it does not reconstruct the original heterogeneous live microbatch or assess every possible batch position/bucket.

Native outputs are float64 after the output transform, while the historical recorder saved float32. Casting native batch16 to the recorded float32 dtype makes all six historical action chunks exactly equal; the residual at most1.176e-7 was serialization rounding.
